Frederick Wildman & Sons Importers
After the repeal of Prohibition, Frederick S. Wildman, a connoisseur of Nato wine in Connecticut, bought the century old bellows and co., An importer of wine and fine-food emporium. In the same year Wildman traveled to the best vineyards in Europe to pursue suppliers and grow his importing company. In a short time, Wildman signed on some of France's best wine producers, many still in Frederick Wildman's portfolio today.
With Wildman in charge, the company grew and prospered. Wildman himself wrote the newsletters and wine notes, always reflecting his personal commitment to the highest quality products for his demanding clientele. The colonel, as he was called, continued to travel to Europe to develop contacts and establish partnerships. When national distillers decided to leave the quality wine business in 1952, the Colonel was able to set up his own company, Frederick Wildman and Sons, Ltd.Champagne Pol Roger, Domaine Armand Rousseau and Château Fuissé were then the pillars of the portfolio and remained when Wildman Colonel retired in 1971, and his company became a subsidiary of Hiram Walker. With Hiram Walker, Frederick Wildman and his sons continued to grow, and the wines of the Rhone by Paul Jaboulet Aîné and several Bordeaux properties were soon added to the rich and prestigious portfolio.

Founded in 1988, Pasternak wine imports is a national importer of fine wines, focused on premium wines, based on terroir from the most influential wine regions, including France, Spain, Italy, Argentina, Chile, New Zealand and California. Headquartered in Harrison, NY, Pasternak Wine Imports distributes fine wine portfolio in all fifty states.
Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant
Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant was born and raised in California. From his youth he remembers that his father and uncle worked for a winery, but has no memory of anyone in his family drinking wine.
Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant family was rich in preachers, too, but to communion they served us grape juice from Welch, though, as Kermit points out, Jesus turned water into wine, not grape juice.
Folio Fine Wine Partners
When they started Folio Fine Wine Partners in 2004, working on folding tables and chairs in their guest house in Napa, they had a vision - that the best wines in the world would come from producers who are family run and managed. An unshakable belief that in every wine they represented would be the only essence of the earth every Steward family. When the family name is on the bottle, there is passion, heritage, history, provenance, integrity and longevity.
Much like a guild, they wanted to provide their distributors and key business partners the best of the world's premier wine regions had to offer without compromising on the support, sales and marketing, PR and compliance that many small producers could not offer. An approach that would have appreciated them partners to their customers of trade and, ultimately, a resource for us wine the most demanding consumers. They are grateful to the Frescobaldi family who were the first family to take the leap of faith with them. Today they are honored to represent the winemaking families from Italy, Spain, France, Argentina and Austria, their business is growing at double digits and they have only just begun.

Grape Expectations is an importer and distributor of California, to the northwest, and international wine. Grape Expectation generally imports artesian wines from cooperative wineries and family and distributes to restaurants and retailers throughout California, Oregon and Washington. When looking for wines, buyers at Grape Expectations are always looking for products that people enjoy every day and buy again and again.
Quintessential Wine Importers
Quintessential is a family owned and managed import, sales and marketing based in Napa, CA. They are dedicated exclusively to multi-generational representation, family owned and managed cellars that have the same passion for winemaking, as they did in marketing and sales of their wines. These producers, from most of the best wine regions in the world, create wines that offer the best, most authentic expression of the terroir from their respective vineyards.
With Quintessential, the Kreps family is realizing their dream of nurturing a roster of multi-generational wineries, owned and managed families whose wines reflect the best, most authentic expression of the terroir from their respective vineyards. Quintessential has become one of the leading companies in the import and marketing of wines in the United States! Between Steve SR., Dennis and Steve Jr., the Kreps bring a combined 78 years of experience in fine wine trading.
Sr. Steve Kreps started in the wine trade in 1973 as a representative and merchandiser. He excelled and quickly became an Area Manager covering ten states. He eventually moved to an import company and quickly moved from Division Manager to the National Sales Manager. In 1988 he founded a brokerage company premium wines and ultra premium wines, covering the Midwest region. Ten years later, Steve formed a prestigious import and marketing company, which eventually sold in 2002 when he collaborated with Dennis to form Quintessential.
Opici Wine Group
Opici Wine Company of New York was founded in 1945. Renowned for its excellent wines and spirits expertise, the NY operation has applied the same principles that have made the Opici Wine Group a success for over 90 years. With its recent expansion in Upstate New York, Opici di NY is destined to become the pre-eminent wine and the company of spirits in the state.
Palm Bay International
As one of North America's premier names imported fine wines and spirits, Palm Bay International has a long established history of introducing distinctive, authentic treasures from the world's premier growing regions for wine and spirits lovers across the United States
Over the past three decades, this family-run company has assembled one of the most valuable and complete portfolios of imported wines and spirits in the United States, which includes some of the most prestigious wineries, distilleries and most popular brands in the industry of the world. Behind this successful story is a well-defined goal of providing high quality, authentic products that represent excellent value. This objective is supported by a committed, attentive and dedicated approach to business and a focus on brand development through long-term relationships with partners, supported by an always excellent service and superior resources.

results.rawContent:
Wine of Rosenthal Wine Merchant
Welcoming Trey Stephenson, Regional Representative
Rosenthal Wine Merchant is a highly-regarded, distinct, and quality-driven portfolio representing, almost exclusively, wines from France and Italy. Their book includes limited-production, estate grown and bottled wines that are made in a classical manner and reflect a specific sense of place. This concept of sense of place, or terroir, became the driving force of the Rosenthal philosophy- the producers they represent must share in their passion of terroir. Rosenthal’s objective from the very beginning was to work as directly as possible with growers and represent wines that are produced in limited quantities, using traditional winemaking methods, and that are made as naturally as possible. Click to read Neal Rosenthal’s definition of the Concept of Terroir.
Neal Rosenthal got into the retail wine business in the late 1970’s and began importing wine shortly thereafter. Today the Rosenthal portfolio includes more than 75 producers from almost every viticultural area of France, a handful of regions in Italy including Piedmont, Tuscany, Umbria, Liguria, and Oltrepo Pavese, as wells as a very small amount from Switzerland, California, and Spain. The wines are selected for concentration, purity of flavors, and clarity of expression. The Rosenthal offerings strike a balance between finesse and power, which results in exceedingly ageworthy wines.
Their high standards and inflexible values set Rosenthal Wine Merchant apart from many in the wine business; they seek out small, family owned and operated producers (as opposed to cooperative, negociant, or commercial ones), they do not follow fads or “hot sources,” they do not purchase wine to “fill a slot” or a missing appellation in their portfolio, they purchase wine from their suppliers year after year, vintage after vintage, regardless of the “quality” of vintage (be it good or bad!), and they visit each grower twice per year to follow the evolution of wines and track development of the estate. To top it all off, their entire sales staff visits each grower so that they can properly communicate the nuance of each estate to their customers.
People ask me all the time what’s my favorite wine, and although I do not have a specific answer to this question, I can say with certainty that Rosenthal wines are my favorites, and the wines that I consume most frequently at home and for pleasure. Commonly we will drink well-known, high-end, high-scoring wines (that are not Rosenthal’s) from regions such as the Rhone Valley, Burgundy, or Piedmont, and almost every time Matt and I agree that Rosenthal’s wines from the same appellation are much better- and in almost every case the Rosenthal wines are a fraction of the production level and a fraction of the cost. In the store there is a barrel by the register with a smattering of wines displayed upon it- if you’ve ever wondered what these wines have in common, it’s that they are imported by RWM and that they are some of my “favorites”.
Tomorrow night for the tasting we will sample three wines from France and three from Italy. We are pleased that Trey Stephenson, South Eastern Representative, will be on-hand to present the wines and answer any questions.
The specific wines for the tasting are:
Chateau La Rame Blanc 2010– Bordeaux, France. Chateau La Rame is among the oldest and most renowned properties in the Sainte Criox du Mont appellation. The estate was purchased by Claude Armand, father of the current owner, Yves Armand. The 20 hectares of Chateau La Rame are set on a clay-limestone soil with an exceptional substratum of fossilized oysters dating from the Tertiary era. The vineyards are planted 75% to Semillon and 25% to Sauvignon Blanc, with vines that average 45 years. The harvest is done entirely by hand over a series of weeks. Bottling is accomplished with no fining and very light filtration. The result is a dry, crisp, enchanting, and aromatic white. Tasting $16.99
Paul Jeune Domaine de Monpertuis Cotes du Rhone 2009– Rhone Valley, France. The Domaine de Monpertuis has been in the hands of the Jeune family for several generations. Each successor has added vineyards and expanded the estate to include today 10 acres of vines amongst 32 separate parcels throughout the confines of Chateauneuf du Pape, as well as Cotes du Rhone and Vin de Pays du Gard. The Cotes du Rhone vineyards are generally between 20 and 60 years and planted almost exclusively to Grenache. The grapes are hand-harvested and fermented separately, whole cluster (with stems), according to varietal. The wine is aged in large foudres and is then bottled without filtration. Tasting $17.99
Jean Claude Thevenet Bourgogne Rouge 2009– Burgundy, France. Jean-Claude Thevenet is a third generation “vigneron” whose winery is located in the heart of the Maconnais in the village of Pierreclos. His grandfather was the winemaker for the Chateau de Pierreclos and his father developed a business as a supplier of rootstock. Today the Thevenets own 25 hectares of vineyards in the adjoining communes of Pierreclos, Prisse, and Rilly Larmartine. The vineyards are planted mostly to Chardonnay (although this is Pinot Noir!); not a single drop of the wine is sold to negociants. The entire harvest is done manually and the wines are made using traditional methods. Tasting $18.99
Luigi Ferrando Erbaluce di Caluso “La Torrazza” 2009– Canavese, Piedmont, Italy (near Val d’Aosta). Luigi Ferrando’s family’s winemaking tradition dates back to 1900; his family is responsible for discovering and preserving local winemaking traditions that may have otherwise been lost. His sons Roberto and Andrea now work with him on the estate, thereby assuring the continuation of the Ferrando tradition. The Canavese is technically part of Piedmont, located near the Val d’Aosta. Erbaluce is an ancient white grape variety originally from the alpine foothills of upper Piedmont. It offers bright acidity, elegant underlying minerality, and an overall structure that makes it the ultimate flexible wine. Tasting $19.99
DeForville Dolcetto d’Alba 2010– Piedmont, Italy. The DeForville family emigrated to Piedmont from Belgium in 1848 and established themselves in the village of Barbaresco in 1860. In the early part of the century the DeForvilles sold their wine in bulk directly to restaurants and retailers, who then bottled the wine. They bottled their first wine in 1940 and today their entire production is bottled at the estate, averaging 100,000 bottles annually. The Dolcetto vines are planted in Barbaresco, in the “cru” vineyard called Lorento. The wine is vinified in the traditional manner and fermented on the skins with extended cuvaison. It is then racked into large oak barrels, where malolactic fermentation takes place. It ages for about nine months prior to bottling. Tasting $16.99
DeForville Langhe Nebbiolo 2009– Piedmont, Italy. The DeForville family began growing the Nebbiolo grape in the village of Barbaresco in 1860. In 1907 Paolo Anfosso married into the DeForville family and took over the reins of the family business. In the early part of the century the DeForvilles sold their wine in bulk directly to restaurants in retailers. They bottled their first wine in 1940. Valter and Paolo Anfosso, sons of Bruno, now manage the estate. The 10 hectare domaine is divided between holdings in Barbaresco and Castagnole Lanze. Within Barbaresco, Nebbiolo is planted in the “cru” vineyards of Rabaja, Lorento, and Pozzo. The Nebbiolo is made in a traditional manner, fermented on the skins through an extended cuvaison, then racked into large oak barrels where malolactic fermentation takes place. The wines of DeForville are particularly ageworthy, and after sufficient bottle age develop complex aromas of fruit, earth, and flowers, that can only result from wines that are vinified in this traditional manner. Tasting $20.99
Much of the information included in the introduction and wine descriptions came from either Rosenthal’s book “Reflections of a Wine Merchant- On a Lifetime in the Vineyards and Cellars of France and Italy” or his website, madrose.com

Belguardo (Mazzei)
Belguardo expresses the classic elegance and aromatics of Maremma.

Borgo Conventi
Borgo Conventi’s white wines hail from the winery’s oldest vineyards in the hills of Collio, a DOC region known for producing exceptional and mineral-driven white wines due to its signature ponca soil series.

Boscarelli
The Poderi Boscarelli estate is the true “cru” of Vino Nobile, nestled among olive groves, broom bushes and oak trees. From this terroir, generations of the De Ferrari Corradi family have committed themselves to bringing forth the aromas and pure character of the Sangiovese grape to reach its most elevated expression.

Purveyors of Pure. Purity drives everything Brendel does. It not only describes the method from which all Brendel wines are made, but the intentions of the people who make them.

Founded by Tom Burgess in 1972, the winery has been continuously owned and operated by the Burgess family until the acquisition by the Lawrence Family this year.

Castello di Fonterutoli (Mazzei)
Established in 1435, the Mazzei family is widely considered one of the founding families of Chianti Classico. Today, the winery remains family-owned after 25 generations and is one of the most awarded wineries in Tuscany. The generational legacy of Mazzei focuses on the balance of history and innovation, carrying forward historic vineyards and winemaking knowledge while embracing research and technology.

Chteau Lascombes
On its hillside at the entrance to Margaux, in the heart of the Médoc, Chteau Lascombes is a Second Growth in the 1855 classification with a long history, characterized by pioneering owners and a terroir that reflects all the characteristics of the appellation

The reputation of Domaine de Montille is patiently earned, with winemaking roots in Burgundy stretching back to 1750. Their internationally renowned wines come from some of the finest vineyards in the Côte-d’Or, with a distinctive, balanced and age-worthy style.

Domaine Roc de l’Abbaye
Domaine Roc de l’Abbaye’s combination of expert winemaking and premium terroir sets them apart, with cellar-worthy wines that showcase the best of Sancerre.

Haynes Vineyard
Haynes vineyard is renowned as the crown jewel of Coombsville, making Chardonnay, Pinot Noir and Syrah with a sense of place. The Lawrence family is only the third family to own the vineyard, which is home to the oldest Pinot Noir and Chardonnay vines in Napa Valley.

Heitz Cellar
Family owned since its founding in 1961, Heitz Cellar’s legacy runs as deep as the roots throughout the Napa Valley; a winery legend that has helped shape the history of Napa Valley winemaking.

Ink Grade
Rugged terrain. Lush foliage. Abundant wildlife. Ink Grade Estate possesses a raw tension that renders fruit of immense intensity and depth. If ever there was a site which imparted a feeling of reverence, Ink Grade is such a place.

Owned and operated by 270 winegrowing families spread across Chablis’ grand and premier cru vineyards, La Chablisienne combines premium quality fruit with a distinctive winemaking style to produce beautiful expressions of this famous AOC.

Legras & Haas
François Legras was born into a family with four centuries of grape growing experience. He founded Legras et Haas in 1991, which is now run by his three children, Rémi, Olivier and Jérôme, who, together, craft genuine and balanced wines.

Matt Taylor Wines
Matt Taylor is a third-generation wine country native with a passion for our region and its breathtaking beauty. He is inspired by biodynamic farming and allowing the fruit to express itself as beautifully as possible, with restraint.

Philipponnat
La Champagne au Coeur—Champagne in our hearts—is the Philipponnat house motto and reﬂects a legacy dating back to 1522 when the family purchased land in the area of Aÿ and Mareuil-sur-Aÿ to grow grapes. Today Philipponnat is lead by 15th generation, Charles Philipponnat, cementing over 500 years as winegrowers in Champagne.

The Moretti Polegato are the largest owners of estate vineyards in Conegliano-Valdobbiadene, showcasing an extreme dedication to elevating the production of Prosecco. Villa Sandi offers a portfolio of fresh and lively Proseccos from DOC Treviso, fruit-driven Prosecco Superiore from Valdobbiadene and Asolo DOCGs, and an elegant and refined offering from Cartizze DOCG, the highest designation of the region.

50 Boutique Wine Importers and Distributors in the USA
29/10/2026 From specialists in natural wines and family estates to regional wholesalers serving independent retailers, these are companies wineries should know when building their U.S. distribution strategy.
For a boutique winery, the right U.S. partner does more than arrange the movement of bottles. It understands the producer, identifies suitable accounts, and gives its sales team a clear reason to recommend the wine.
That makes portfolio fit essential. A specialist in Italian family estates may be well suited to an unfamiliar indigenous variety. A natural-wine importer may place particular importance on farming and cellar practices. A regional distributor may offer the focused market coverage a small winery can realistically support.
The following guide brings together 50 boutique and specialist wine importers and distributors serving the United States. Some are small businesses with tightly focused portfolios; others are larger companies that maintain a strong commitment to independent producers.
Official websites and company portfolio information were checked for this article on October 28, 2026. This is an editorial guide, not a sales ranking. Importing and wholesale distribution are different services, and inclusion does not mean a company is currently accepting new producers.
Importers With a Strong Grower and Estate Focus
1. Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant
Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant imports wines from France and Italy, with a portfolio spanning celebrated regions and less familiar appellations. Its producer-centered approach makes it an important reference for wineries studying specialist importing. Producers should examine the existing growers and regional coverage before proposing a fit.
2. Rosenthal Wine Merchant
Rosenthal Wine Merchant emphasizes small, family-owned estates and wines that communicate their origins. Its portfolio includes producers from France, Italy, Switzerland, Spain, and Austria. For wineries, the central question is whether their vineyards, winemaking, and regional identity complement the merchant’s established approach.
3. Louis/Dressner Selections
Louis/Dressner Selections has longstanding relationships with independent growers and a strong interest in farming and winemaking practices. Its website provides extensive producer information and harvest reports. Wineries researching the business should be ready to discuss their work in the vineyard and cellar in detail.
4. Skurnik Wines & Spirits
Skurnik Wines & Spirits combines national importing with direct wholesale distribution in selected states. Its portfolio includes boutique producers from around the world. Suppliers should distinguish between a national import relationship and a proposal for a specific wholesale market, then approach the relevant team accordingly.
5. T. Edward Wines & Spirits
T. Edward Wines & Spirits began with boutique estates and continues to emphasize family-owned producers, craftsmanship, and authenticity. Its business includes importing and distribution. A winery’s introduction should explain the people behind the wine, its production philosophy, and its commercial role within the portfolio.
6. Bowler Wine
Bowler Wine is a New York-based importer and distributor focused on naturally made, small-production wines. Its selection emphasizes personality, regional character, and family growers. Wineries should research both its direct producer relationships and the other import portfolios it represents before making an introduction. NYC Wine Spirits Importer Distributor
7. European Cellars
European Cellars imports wines from family-owned properties practicing responsible viticulture. Its roots in France and Spain have expanded into other origins. Producers should assess how their wines express place and whether they add a distinct regional or stylistic contribution to the existing selection.
8. De Maison Selections
De Maison Selections is a national importer with a strong commitment to artisanal properties, regional heritage, and producer independence. Its business distinguishes national importing from direct distribution through De Maison East. Wineries should establish which relationship they are seeking before presenting their portfolio.
9. Polaner Selections
Polaner Selections combines established reference-point producers with smaller wineries, indigenous varieties, and less familiar regions. Its selection includes traditional producers and growers using organic or biodynamic practices. A compelling proposal should explain both the wine’s individuality and its value at the intended selling price.
10. Martine’s Wines
Martine’s Wines operates as an importer and wholesaler, with producer profiles and current wine information on its website. Its portfolio includes wines from established French regions and distinctive estates such as Domaine des Ardoisières. Suppliers should study the relevant regional selection before proposing additional representation. Importer & Wholesaler since 1979
Natural Wine and Small-Production Specialists
11. Jenny & François Selections
Jenny & François Selections focuses on natural wines from small growers. Its philosophy considers both vineyard practices and cellar methods. Producers researching the company should prepare a transparent account of farming, fermentation, additions, and production, alongside the practical information needed to evaluate a U.S. launch.
12. Zev Rovine Selections
Zev Rovine Selections works with growers who farm organically or biodynamically and favor minimal intervention in the cellar. Its producer list spans numerous countries. Wineries should assess philosophical fit and regional overlap, rather than assume a natural-wine identity alone creates an opening in the portfolio.
13. Selection Massale
Selection Massale imports natural wines from small wineries, emphasizing precision and drinkability. Its stated approach favors naturally fermented wines and growers working largely organically or biodynamically. Producers should explain how their practices translate into the wine’s character and consistency.
14. José Pastor Selections
José Pastor Selections champions small growers and traditionally made wines, with deep Spanish roots and a portfolio extending to other origins. Its selection includes regional grapes and distinctive vineyard environments. Wineries should explain what makes their wines an authentic expression of their particular place.
15. SelectioNaturel
SelectioNaturel specializes in Italian wines made in small quantities using natural and traditional methods. Its narrow focus makes regional and philosophical alignment especially important. Italian producers should study the represented growers and explain what their wines contribute beyond an appealing production story.
16. Vom Boden
Vom Boden focuses on small estates and growers whose work or locations sit outside the obvious mainstream. Its website includes current material on German wine. Producers considering the company should research its selection carefully and explain the vineyard, regional, and stylistic reasons their wines belong in that conversation.
17. Schatzi Wines
Schatzi Wines emphasizes the connection between growers and wine drinkers, with authenticity, sustainability, and terroir central to its approach. Its portfolio is built around producer relationships. Wineries should prepare clear information about their farming, wines, and expectations for a long-term importing partnership.
18. Olmstead Wine Co.
Olmstead Wine Co. is a Massachusetts distributor explicitly focused on natural wine. It provides a regional prospect for producers and importers whose wines fit that category. Suppliers should examine the portfolio and establish the current route for introducing new wines to the team.
19. Walden Selections
Walden Selections is a Washington State importer and distributor of wine and other beverages. It also appears in SelectioNaturel’s distribution network. Producers researching Washington should review the existing selection and discuss the specific importing or wholesale services required.
20. Nomadic Distribution
Nomadic Distribution presents itself as an importer and distributor of organic and natural wines. Its website includes producer information and a natural-wine shop. Suppliers should begin by reviewing the current producer list and confirming the relevant markets, portfolio needs, and submission process.
Regional and Country Specialists
21. The Piedmont Guy
The Piedmont Guy is a U.S.-based importer specializing in family-owned wineries from Piedmont. Its focused portfolio makes it particularly relevant to producers from that region. A pitch should explain the winery’s local identity, varieties, and position alongside the estates already represented.
22. Oliver McCrum Wines & Spirits
Oliver McCrum Wines & Spirits imports small-production Italian wines and operates distribution activities. Its stated preferences include clarity, freshness, indigenous varieties, and transparent winemaking. Producers should connect those characteristics with pricing and an account proposition that a sales team can readily explain.
23. Dalla Terra Italian Wine & Spirits
Dalla Terra describes its business as a national agent and direct importer for a select group of artisan, family-owned Italian wineries and spirits producers. Italian suppliers should understand its direct-import model and assess the existing regional portfolio before approaching the company.
24. Indigenous Selections
Indigenous Selections represents a curated group of Italian wineries selected for authenticity and regional character. Its portfolio covers origins including Piedmont, Tuscany, Veneto, Campania, Sicily, and Friuli. Producers should show how their wines offer a distinctive expression within the relevant region and price segment.
25. Porto Vino
Porto Vino maintains a French and Italian portfolio that includes producers from regions such as the Loire, Burgundy, Piedmont, and Sicily. Its website provides a detailed producer list. Suppliers should examine that regional coverage and explain where their wines add a meaningful point of difference.
26. North Berkeley Imports
North Berkeley Imports sources wines from France and Italy, combining importing with selected direct-market portfolios and distribution partners. Its offer reaches restaurants, wine shops, and collectors. Producers should distinguish the national portfolio opportunity from the company’s specific wholesale-market activities.
27. Michael Corso Selections
Michael Corso Selections is a specialist importer with a strong French wine focus. Its portfolio includes regions such as Alsace, Burgundy, the Loire, and the Rhône. Producers should present their regional credentials alongside a clear explanation of value and likely U.S. positioning.
28. Charles Neal Selections
Charles Neal Selections is a San Francisco-based importer and distributor with French wines and a substantial spirits selection. Its specialist approach makes it relevant to producers with a clear regional identity. Suppliers should explain the wine’s quality and commercial relevance without relying on small production as the sole selling point.
29. Brazos Wine Imports
Brazos Wine Imports focuses on artisan wines from Argentina, Chile, and Uruguay. Its stated interests include estate-grown, small-production wines that express specific places. South American producers should prepare detailed vineyard information and explain how the wines differ from more familiar market offerings.
30. Little Peacock Imports
Little Peacock Imports emphasizes a curated selection of family wineries, with producer listings covering Australia, France, Italy, and New Zealand. Its positioning combines discovery with commercial performance. Suppliers should explain why the wine is distinctive and how it can earn repeat purchases.
Curated Importers With Broader Portfolios
31. Grand Cru Selections
Grand Cru Selections is a New York-based importer and distributor with a strong fine-wine portfolio. Its producer information covers Champagne, Burgundy, and other regions. Wineries should research the existing estates closely and present a precise case for stylistic, regional, and commercial fit.
32. Coeur Wine Co.
Coeur Wine Co. emphasizes long-term producer relationships and wines it considers honest and authentic. Its website provides producer information and distribution partners. Suppliers should focus their introduction on the wine’s quality, its intended customer, and the practical foundations of a lasting relationship.
33. Communal Brands
Communal Brands combines production, importing, and distribution, with an emphasis on environmentally conscious wines and contemporary presentation. Its offer includes alternative formats such as boxed wine. Wineries should consider how product format, quality, and customer occasion work together within this business model.
34. Vine Connections
Vine Connections imports and distributes wines from family producers in origins including Argentina, Chile, Italy, France, and California. Its website provides trade tools such as technical sheets and shelf talkers. Producers should prepare a similarly complete set of materials when seeking representation. Global Wine, Sake & Spirits Importer
35. Massanois
Massanois is a national importer with direct distribution in selected markets. Its portfolio emphasizes quality-driven, family-owned wineries and distilleries. Suppliers should determine whether they need importing, direct wholesale distribution, or both, then tailor the proposal to the appropriate operation.
36. Banville Wine Merchants
Banville Wine Merchants combines national importing with wholesale operations in selected U.S. markets. Its approach centers on a selective, quality-focused portfolio. Producers should distinguish the national import opportunity from local distribution and identify the specific customer and price tier their wines would serve.
37. Regal Wine Imports
Regal Wine Imports maintains importing and distribution activities across wine and other beverage categories. Its website includes producer portfolios, trade information, and recent company content. Wineries should examine the relevant portfolio and market operation before proposing a new regional or stylistic addition.
38. Artisans & Vines
Artisans & Vines sources wines from Europe and several New World origins, emphasizing terroir and value. Its business includes importing, marketing, and distribution relationships. Suppliers should clarify the proposed territory and responsibilities, then connect their wine’s identity with a realistic market-development plan.
39. Wine Traditions
Wine Traditions seeks independent growers whose wines express their vineyards and offer accessible value. It operates as a national imp

results.rawContent:
Kermit Lynch was raised in the wine region of San Luis Obispo, but for forty years his name has become synonymous with French and Italian wines. In 1972, with a $5,000 loan and some raw gumption, this writer/musician-turned-wine-retailer opened Kermit Lynch Wine Merchant with thirty-five cases of wine stacked on the floor. Convinced early on that the wines of Europe were better suited to his palate than those of California, Kermit has become an advocate for authentic wines that express their terroir. He has had so much success at bringing notice to small, artisan producers that he has won two James Beard awards and was knighted by the French government in 2005 with the prestigious Legion of Honor. In addition to having three books published, Adventures on the Wine Route (1988, Veuve Cliquot Wine Book of the Year), Inspiring Thirst (2004), and the 25th Anniversary Edition: Adventures on the Wine Route (2013), his passion for roots music has driven him to record four CDs so far. Kermit and his wife, photographer Gail Skoff, divide their time between Provence, France, and Berkeley, California.
Importers
>
Kermit Lynch

IPO Wines

IPO Wines was founded in 2006 in New York City with the mission of bringing small-production, terroir-driven wines that represent the best their region has to offer to our customers. Our goal is to share our producer's history, legacy, and philosophy. Like loyal warriors we thrive by being our producer's voices in our urban arena. We seek to build relationships with those that share the same vision and passion. Most importantly, our goal is to service our customers with a dedicated sense of duty, responsiveness, care and diligence, for they are the reason we exist. We are committed to connecting our customers to more than just wine, but to also connect them with the experience the culture of wine brings to us.
Jon-David Headrick

Jon-David Headrick Selections is a American importer of small French wine properties, specializing in the wines of the Loire Valley in France. The Loire is special. These are wines, when produced from older vines and crafted by artisans, that define elegance and restraint in the glass. These are wines that deserve to be tasted by lovers of wine.
European Cellars (Eric Solomon)

From the founding of European Cellars in 1989, Eric Salomon has championed unheralded wine growing regions and promoted young, innovative winemakers. His initial focus was France where he was an early proponent of the wines of the Rhône, the Languedoc and the Roussillon. His growing reputation in Europe as a new, dynamic and successful importer prompted Daphne Glorian to send him, unsolicited, a sample of her wine, Clos Erasmus in 1993. This event led not only to their eventual marriage, but an equally exciting portfolio of Spanish wines.
Circo Vino

Founded in 2009, Circo Vino, loosely translated as “Wine Circus,” is a fine wine importer that offers serious artistry and joyful pleasure in our portfolio selection. Specializing in wines from unique terroirs, crafted by wine farmers who take great care from vineyard to table, our wines bring stories, education and experiences. We invite you to join our circus of sublime wine – a collaborative performance between mother nature, the grower and you.
Coalla Gourmet

Coalla Gourmet was founded more than 50 years ago as a supermarket in Gijón (Asturias) in Northern Spain. At the end of the 20th century, it started distributing wines regionally, then importing wines and distributing them nationally. An initial facilitator of Equipo Navazos, the company became the exclusive exporter for their wines as soon as the project gained recognition beyond Spain.
Vila Viniteca

Vila Viniteca is one of the most renowned Spanish wine distributors in the restaurant and retail trade and among the most prestigious Wine Merchants in Europe. The company was founded in 1932 and now is in its third generation as a family-run business. As well as being a distributor, importer and exporter, Vila Viniteca sells to the public and trade. Furthermore, it participates in numerous wine making projects with legendary Spanish winemakers. With more than 8,000 references in its portfolio, Vila Viniteca exclusively represents more than 200 cellars around the world, including premier brands at international level.
Karolus Wine Imports

Karolus Wine Imports is a U.S. importer specializing in wines from the revered Burgundian estate, Bonneau du Martray. The name ‘Karolus’ pays homage to Charlemagne, or Charles the Great, known in Latin as ‘Karolus Magnus.' For Karolus, maintaining the quality of the wines we import is paramount, and it is considered in every step of the journey from Burgundy. Though nothing can compare to drinking Corton-Charlemagne while overlooking the beautiful limestone Hill of Corton in Burgundy, we aim to ensure that each bottle tastes as it was intended no matter where it is finally opened.
